question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says "When a casting door refuses a red's ticket (RedTicketRefused), run_proof raises an unticketed trouble naming the door and its lacks instead of writing a ticket", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline states 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...unless one is already open for it.' The ticket adds a new exception case—'unless the door refuses'—where no ticket is written at all, only a trouble is recorded. The outline's guarantee that a ticket is written for every new red no longer holds when the door refuses. The ticket's own constraint acknowledges this: 'the trouble never stands in for the ticket outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 requires...the red still needs its ticket.'). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands, and the ticket does not add an exception to it: a door already refuses red casts today (measured on akiendell 2026-11-23, three sorted berths and no ticket), and that refusal is a defect against 9.4.2.3.7.5 that currently leaves no trace. The ticket makes the defect visible, a trouble naming the door and lacks that clears only when the red is ticketed. The intention is reworded to say so.
